stories.headline: Middle East tensions mount as Houthi attacks target Saudi infrastructure and crude prices surge
stories.body:
Houthi forces attacked a military airbase and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia. The missile and drone attack on Monday targeted aircraft hangars. It also targeted ammunition depots at the Khamis Mushait military airbase in southern Saudi Arabia. The Saudi-led coalition said 13 civilians were injured in Saudi Arabia. They were injured after a wave of ballistic missile and drone attacks by Houthi forces. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said Saudi warplanes carried out 58 air raids across six provinces within 24 hours. On Sunday, Iran-aligned Houthi forces captured the strategic island of Perim in the Bab al-Mandab strait.

Oil prices rose sharply after the attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure. Brent crude futures rose $1.24 to $106.93 a barrel on Tuesday. On Monday, Brent crude had surged to more than $108.50 a barrel. That increase represented a 3.7 percent daily rise. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures rose $1.29 to $102.65 a barrel on Tuesday. The yield on 10-year U.S. Treasury bonds reached 5 percent on Monday. That was its highest level since October 2023.

Saudi Arabia operates the East-West pipeline. The pipeline transports oil across the country to the Red Sea port of Yanbu. This route allows exports to bypass the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran imposed a virtual blockade on the Strait of Hormuz in March 2026. That blockade came after U.S.-Israeli military strikes on Iran on February 28. Commodity vessel transits through the Strait of Hormuz dropped over the weekend. Transits fell to fewer than 10 per day. This compares to a 10-day average of 14 transits.

Security incidents also took place at sea. U.S. Central Command said an Iranian drone struck the Panama-flagged tanker El Gaia off Oman over the weekend. An Iranian missile had already hit the vessel last month. U.S. Central Command rejected Iranian claims that the tanker hit a naval mine. Thirteen of the 14 Indian crew members aboard El Gaia were rescued off Oman. One Indian crew member remained missing.

Diplomatic efforts faced delays. Mohsen Rezaei is the secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council. Rezaei said Iran will not enter talks with the United States until Tehran's conditions are met.

claims.text: Brent crude futures rose $1.24 to $106.93 a barrel on Tuesday following attacks on Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure.
Houthi forces launched a missile and drone attack targeting aircraft hangars and ammunition depots at the Khamis Mushait military airbase in southern Saudi Arabia on Monday.
The Saudi-led coalition stated that 13 civilians were injured in Saudi Arabia following a wave of ballistic missile and drone attacks by Houthi forces.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree stated that Saudi warplanes carried out 58 air raids across six provinces within a 24-hour period.
Iran-aligned Houthi forces captured the strategic island of Perim in the Bab al-Mandab strait on Sunday.
Brent crude surged to more than $108.50 a barrel on Monday, representing a 3.7 percent daily increase.
U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures rose $1.29 to $102.65 a barrel on Tuesday.
The yield on 10-year U.S. Treasury bonds reached 5 percent on Monday, marking its highest level since October 2023.
Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline transports oil across the country to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, allowing exports to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.
Tehran imposed a virtual blockade on the Strait of Hormuz in March 2026 following U.S.-Israeli military strikes on Iran on February 28.
Commodity vessel transits through the Strait of Hormuz dropped to fewer than 10 per day over the weekend, compared to a 10-day average of 14.

U.S. Central Command rejected Iranian claims that the Panama-flagged tanker El Gaia hit a naval mine, stating it was struck by an Iranian drone off the coast of Oman over the weekend after being hit by an Iranian missile last month.
Thirteen of the 14 Indian crew members aboard the oil tanker El Gaia were rescued off the coast of Oman, while one Indian crew member remained missing.
Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, stated that Iran will not enter talks with the United States until Tehran's conditions are met.

stories.headline: Russian drone strikes Ukrainian train station as diplomatic activity continues
stories.body:
Russian forces struck a Ukrainian train station near the Polish border. A Russian drone hit Yahodyn train station on Sunday. The strike happened shortly after a train carrying former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson departed. Russian forces also struck two cargo vessels in the Black Sea on Monday. In addition, a British military member died in a non-hostile traffic incident in Ukraine on Saturday. Polish Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said Poland recovered a suspected Russian military drone from the Baltic Sea. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte promised more support for Ukraine and stronger defenses near Poland.

U.S. President Donald Trump posted that Ukraine and Russia agreed not to hit energy targets. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine will halt strikes on Russian energy targets if Russia stops attacking Ukrainian energy sites. Kyrylo Budanov heads the Ukrainian president's office. Budanov said Ukraine is preparing for trilateral talks with Russia in October. A summer 2026 poll by the Kyiv International Institute of Sociology showed 60 percent of Ukrainians support freezing frontline fighting for security guarantees. European Union nations extended a deadline to renew Russian sanctions by one week after France sought to remove tycoon Alisher Usmanov from the list.

claims.text: A Russian drone struck Yahodyn train station near the Polish border on Sunday shortly after a train carrying former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson departed.
Russian forces struck two cargo vessels in the Black Sea on Monday, according to reports from Interfax.
A member of the British armed forces died in a non-hostile road traffic incident in Ukraine on Saturday.
Polish Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz stated that the Polish military recovered a suspected Russian military drone from the Baltic Sea near Jaroslawiec.
NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte pledged increased support for Ukraine and strengthened defenses along NATO's eastern border following Russian drone strikes near Poland.
U.S. President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that Ukraine and Russia agreed not to strike each other's energy infrastructure.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine is willing to halt strikes on Russian critical infrastructure if Russia stops its attacks on Ukrainian energy targets.
Kyrylo Budanov, head of the Ukrainian president's office, stated that Ukraine is preparing for a new round of US-mediated trilateral talks with Russia in October.
A summer 2026 poll by the Kyiv International Institute of Sociology found that 60 percent of Ukrainians support freezing frontline fighting in exchange for security guarantees.
European Union member states extended the deadline for renewing sanctions against Russia by one week following a push by France to remove Uzbek-Russian tycoon Alisher Usmanov from the blacklist.

stories.headline: Tech leaders call for pause in AI progress while Trump rejects safety rules
stories.body:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published an essay urging a slowdown in artificial intelligence development. Amodei titled the essay 'We Must Pace the Frontier'. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis, and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk supported the call to slow AI progress. Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark told the BBC that a third-party AI kill switch may be needed. But U.S. President Donald Trump dismissed regulation efforts. Trump posted that calls for guardrails are a 'sick conspiracy'.

Markets reacted to the safety warnings. Nvidia shares fell 3.3 percent on Monday. SoftBank stock dropped 13 percent. Anthropic and OpenAI filed documentation one week apart to list on public markets. Both target valuations above $1 trillion. OpenAI and Google signed defense agreements with the Pentagon in February 2026. Those deals occurred after Anthropic refused to allow its models for autonomous weapons or mass surveillance. In legal news, Elon Musk's X Corp and SpaceXAI dropped antitrust claims against Apple regarding ChatGPT. They had sued in August 2025 over iPhone integration. They are continuing their lawsuit against OpenAI.

claims.text: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published an essay titled 'We Must Pace the Frontier' urging a slowdown in artificial intelligence development.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis, and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk expressed support for Dario Amodei's call to slow AI development.
Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark told the BBC that a third-party AI 'kill switch' may be required to prevent potential catastrophes.
U.S. President Donald Trump dismissed efforts to regulate artificial intelligence, posting that calls for guardrails are a 'sick conspiracy'.
Shares in Nvidia fell 3.3 percent and SoftBank stock slumped 13 percent on Monday following tech leaders' public warnings regarding AI safety.
Anthropic and OpenAI filed SEC documentation one week apart to list on public markets at target valuations exceeding $1 trillion.
OpenAI and Google signed agreements with the U.S. Pentagon in February 2026 after Anthropic refused to allow its AI models to be used for autonomous lethal weapons or mass surveillance.
Elon Musk's X Corp and SpaceXAI dropped their antitrust claims against Apple over its ChatGPT integration while continuing their lawsuit against OpenAI.
X Corp and SpaceXAI filed an antitrust lawsuit in August 2025 alleging Apple and OpenAI colluded to make ChatGPT the exclusive AI chatbot integrated into the iPhone operating system.

stories.headline: Aliko Dangote launches $1.6 billion public stock offering for Nigerian refinery
stories.body:
Nigerian industrialist Aliko Dangote launched a public offering for the Dangote Petroleum Refinery. The share sale aims to raise $1.6 billion from retail investors across Africa. The offering opened on the Nigerian exchange. Buying will run until October 13. The IPO offers a minimum bundle of 10 shares for 5,250 naira, or about $4. Dangote will keep an 87 percent ownership stake after the offering.

The refinery supplies more than 70 percent of Nigeria's domestic energy consumption. The company generated an after-tax profit of $1.82 billion in the first half of 2026. That profit came after a $476 million loss in 2025. Dangote Industries plans to use IPO funds to support a $14.3 billion expansion. The expansion aims to boost refining capacity from 700,000 to 1.4 million barrels per day. Dangote also plans to launch an oil processing plant in Kenya with eastern African governments. He plans to build a $17 billion energy complex in Lamu, Kenya, with a capacity of 700,000 barrels per day.

The initial public offering for the Dangote Petroleum Refinery opened on the Nigerian exchange with subscription running until October 13.
The Dangote Petroleum Refinery IPO offers retail investors a minimum 10-share bundle for 5,250 naira ($4).
Aliko Dangote will retain an 87 percent ownership stake in the Dangote Petroleum Refinery following the public offering.
The Dangote Petroleum Refinery supplies more than 70 percent of Nigeria's domestic energy consumption.
The Dangote Petroleum Refinery generated an after-tax profit of $1.82 billion in the first half of 2026 after posting a $476 million loss in 2025.
Dangote Industries plans to use funds raised from the IPO to support a $14.3 billion expansion aimed at increasing refining capacity from 700,000 to 1.4 million barrels per day.
Aliko Dangote plans to launch an oil processing plant in Kenya in partnership with eastern African governments.
Aliko Dangote plans to build a $17 billion energy complex in Lamu, Kenya, with a refining capacity of 700,000 barrels per day.

stories.headline: Leaders from Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland sign pact seeking UK independence
stories.body:
Scottish First Minister John Swinney signed an agreement calling for independence from the United Kingdom. Welsh First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth and Northern Ireland First Minister Michelle O'Neill also signed the deal in Cardiff. Sinn Féin president Mary Lou McDonald signed the memorandum alongside them. The joint statement from the SNP, Plaid Cymru, and Sinn Féin said Europe is their home. It declared that their nations belong in the European Union. Plaid Cymru won the May Senedd elections. That victory ended Labour's continuous governance of Wales since 1999.

Opponents criticized the meeting. Conservative shadow Scottish secretary Harriet Cross called it a 'separatist summit' and a photo call. Downing Street said UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is focusing on the cost-of-living crisis instead of constitutional debates. Burnham rejected calls for another Scottish independence referendum before the next general election.

claims.text: Scottish First Minister John Swinney, Welsh First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth, and Northern Ireland First Minister Michelle O'Neill signed a Memorandum of Understanding in Cardiff calling for independence from the United Kingdom.
Sinn Féin president Mary Lou McDonald signed the Cardiff memorandum alongside the first ministers of Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.
The joint statement signed by the SNP, Plaid Cymru, and Sinn Féin declared that Europe is their common home and that the future of their nations belongs in the European Union.
Plaid Cymru's victory in the May Senedd elections ended Labour's continuous governance of Wales that began with devolution in 1999.
Conservative shadow Scottish secretary Harriet Cross characterized the Cardiff meeting as a 'separatist summit' and a 'performative photo call'.
Downing Street stated that UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is focused on tackling the cost-of-living crisis rather than engaging in constitutional debates.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham rejected calls to hold another Scottish independence referendum before the next general election.

vocab.meaning: a direct vote by the public on a single political issue

stories.headline: BJP leads seats in Rajasthan municipal elections as counting disputes trigger repolls
stories.body:
The Bharatiya Janata Party won the most seats in Rajasthan local body elections. The BJP won 4,179 wards out of 10,235 declared wards. Congress won 3,613 wards. Independent candidates won 2,273 wards. Over 1.44 crore voters were eligible to vote across 309 local bodies in two phases on September 9 and 11. Rajasthan Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra said the BJP's overall lead was under one percentage point. Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised the BJP victory on X.

The BJP secured majorities in four municipal corporations: Jaipur, Bhilwara, Kota, and Udaipur. The BJP won 55 out of 100 wards in Kota. In Bundi, three independents joined the BJP to give the party a majority. Congress won the council in Jhalawar, a former stronghold of former chief minister Vasundhara Raje. Congress also won 42 of 80 wards in Bikaner. In Ajmer, Congress won 37 wards, BJP won 32, and independents won 11. The Aam Aadmi Party won its first municipal body in Baran. In Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma's home area of Bharatpur, independents won 36 wards, BJP won 20, and Congress won seven. In Jodhpur, BJP and Congress tied with 44 wards each. In Jaipur, 21-year-old Congress candidate Faiz Hasan won Ward 71 with 5,426 votes.

Technical problems delayed final outcomes in some places. The State Election Commission postponed leadership votes in Jaipur, Jodhpur, Kota, and Suket due to voting machine glitches. Congress candidate Laxmi Sharma protested outside JDB College in Kota after Ward 87 counting stopped. The commission ordered repolling at 10 polling stations for September 16, with counting on September 17.

claims.text: The Bharatiya Janata Party emerged as the single largest party in Rajasthan's urban local body elections, winning 4,179 wards out of 10,235 declared wards.
In the Rajasthan urban local body polls, Congress won 3,613 wards and independent candidates won 2,273 wards.
More than 1.44 crore voters were eligible to vote across 309 urban local bodies in Rajasthan in two phases on September 9 and 11.
Rajasthan Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra stated that the BJP's lead over Congress in this election was less than one percentage point.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailed the BJP's victory in Rajasthan civic polls on X, describing it as proof of the 'victory of truth over the echo of falsehood'.
The BJP secured clear majorities in four municipal corporations in Rajasthan: Jaipur, Bhilwara, Kota, and Udaipur.
The BJP secured 55 out of 100 wards in the Kota Municipal Corporation election to cross the majority threshold.
In Bundi, three independent candidates—Prabhat Devi, Aatmaram Chopdar, and Vishal Sharma—joined the BJP after the election, giving the party a full majority.
In Jhalawar, Congress won the municipal council, taking control of a former stronghold of former chief minister Vasundhara Raje.
Congress won 42 of 80 wards in Bikaner Municipal Corporation to secure a majority.
In Ajmer, Congress emerged as the largest party winning 37 of 80 wards, while BJP won 32 and Independents won 11.
The Aam Aadmi Party made its political debut in Rajasthan by winning control of its maiden municipal body in Baran.
In Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma's home turf of Bharatpur, independents won 36 wards, BJP won 20 wards, and Congress won seven wards.
In Jodhpur Municipal Corporation, BJP and Congress tied with 44 wards each in the 100-member body.
21-year-old Congress candidate Faiz Hasan won Ward 71 in Jaipur Municipal Corporation with 5,426 votes.
The State Election Commission postponed chairperson and deputy chairperson elections in Jaipur, Jodhpur, Kota municipal corporations, and Suket municipality due to EVM technical glitches.
Congress candidate Laxmi Sharma sat on a dharna outside JDB College in Kota demanding transparency after counting in Ward 87 was put on hold due to EVM malfunction.
The State Election Commission ordered repolling at 10 polling stations in Jaipur, Jodhpur, Kota, and Suket for September 16, with counting scheduled for September 17.

stories.headline: Amit Shah plans Uniform Civil Code across 21 states as allies urge consultation
stories.body:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah said he expects a Uniform Civil Code in 21 BJP-NDA ruled states before 2029. Shah made the statement in Mumbai. Uttarakhand passed its Uniform Civil Code Act in February 2024 and enforced it in January 2025. Gujarat passed its code in March 2026. Assam passed its bill in May 2026 while exempting Scheduled Tribes. Madhya Pradesh passed its bill in July 2026. Committees are drafting legislation in Maharashtra, West Bengal, and Chhattisgarh.

Coalition partners urged caution. TDP leader Lavu Sri Krishna Devarayalu said his party will consult stakeholders before adopting the code in Andhra Pradesh. JD(U) leader Sanjay Jha said he will meet Shah to discuss the issue. LJP chief Chirag Paswan called for public consultations. HAM leader Santosh Kumar Suman expected good elements in the proposal. But JD(U) MLA Shyam Rajak said the code will never take effect in Bihar. Opposition leaders strongly opposed the plan. RJD spokesperson Shakti Yadav said his party will block the code in Bihar. AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi said the proposal targets Muslims and imposes Hindu law.

claims.text: Union Home Minister Amit Shah stated in Mumbai that he is confident the Uniform Civil Code will be introduced in 21 BJP-NDA ruled states before 2029.
Uttarakhand passed the Uniform Civil Code Act in February 2024 and fully enforced it on January 27, 2025.
The Gujarat Legislative Assembly passed the Gujarat Uniform Civil Code in March 2026.
The Assam Legislative Assembly passed the Uniform Civil Code, Assam, Bill in May 2026, while exempting members of Scheduled Tribes.
The Madhya Pradesh Legislative Assembly passed the Madhya Pradesh Uniform Civil Code Bill in July 2026.
Maharashtra, West Bengal, and Chhattisgarh have formed committees to draft Uniform Civil Code legislation.
TDP parliamentary party leader Lavu Sri Krishna Devarayalu stated that TDP will involve various stakeholders before adopting the Uniform Civil Code in Andhra Pradesh.
JD(U) working president Sanjay Jha stated that he will meet Union Home Minister Amit Shah to discuss the Uniform Civil Code issue.
LJP (Ram Vilas) chief Chirag Paswan called for the Uniform Civil Code proposal to be made public and undergo comprehensive consultation before his party states its position.
HAM (S) national president Santosh Kumar Suman stated that if Home Minister Amit Shah proposed UCC, there must be good things in it, and alliance leaders would be taken into confidence.
JD(U) MLA Shyam Rajak stated that the Uniform Civil Code will never be implemented in Bihar at any cost.
RJD spokesperson Shakti Yadav stated that the RJD will never allow the Uniform Civil Code to be implemented in Bihar.
AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi stated that a Uniform Civil Code is not about equality but about targeting Muslims and imposing Hindu law on non-Hindus.

stories.headline: CBI opens probe into death of Disha Salian following High Court order
stories.body:
The Central Bureau of Investigation opened a criminal case to investigate the death of Disha Salian. Salian worked as a celebrity manager. She died on June 8, 2020, after falling from a 14th floor in Mumbai. Actor Sushant Singh Rajput was found dead six days later. The Bombay High Court directed the CBI on September 2 to open the probe based on a statement from her father, Satish Salian. Judges said police failures and discrepancies raised serious questions. Satish Salian gave a new statement to the CBI on September 12.

The CBI registered the FIR on September 13 under sections for gang rape, murder, and evidence destruction. Defense lawyer Nilesh Ojha said the FIR cites several penal sections. The case mentions Aaditya Thackeray, Dino Morea, Rhea Chakraborty, Uddhav Thackeray, and Sachin Vaze for investigation. None are named as formal accused. The FIR alleges severe contradictions and record suppression regarding Salian's phone. Politician Supriya Sule expressed surprise at the new probe after the case was previously closed. AIMIM leader Waris Pathan urged political parties to let courts decide the matter.

claims.text: The Central Bureau of Investigation registered an FIR on September 13 to probe the death of celebrity manager Disha Salian under IPC sections for gang rape, murder, and destruction of evidence.
Disha Salian died on June 8, 2020, after falling from the 14th floor of a residential building in Mumbai.
Actor Sushant Singh Rajput was found dead at his residence on June 14, 2020, six days after Disha Salian's death.
A division bench of the Bombay High Court directed the CBI on September 2 to register an FIR into Disha Salian's death based on a statement by her father, Satish Salian.
The Bombay High Court stated that the failure of Mumbai Police to register an FIR for six years raised questions and noted glaring discrepancies in the prior investigation.
Satish Salian recorded a fresh statement at the CBI's Bandra-Kurla Complex office in Mumbai on September 12.
Satish Salian's lawyer Nilesh Ojha stated that the CBI FIR invokes IPC Sections 376D, 302, 201, 217, 218, and 120B.

The CBI FIR mentions several individuals whose roles require investigation, including Aaditya Thackeray, Dino Morea, Rhea Chakraborty, Uddhav Thackeray, and Sachin Vaze, though no one is formally named as an accused.
The CBI FIR alleges extraordinary contradictions and suppression of records regarding the seizure and use of Disha Salian's mobile phone.
NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule expressed surprise at the CBI registering an FIR, noting that the same government had previously closed the case.
AIMIM leader Waris Pathan stated that the Disha Salian case should not be given political color and should be left for the court to decide.

vocab.meaning: illogical differences or inconsistencies between facts or records
the deliberate hiding or withholding of information or evidence
